file_reviews.assessment: Full manuscript inspected. Section 3 establishes Corollary LpC-C1 (circulation characterization of exactness) and Corollary L1C-C1 (general graph exactness criterion). Section 4.2 establishes Theorem LpC-T4P (strict convexity, unique quotient minimizer, and nonlinear graph p-Laplacian). Section 4.3 establishes Theorem LpC-T4H (weighted L2 Hodge-Helmholtz decomposition and Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse potential).

Ledger entries read. Line 19 LpC-C1 (vanishing circulation pairings characterize exactness for all p), line 20 L1C-C1 (general graph exactness criterion), line 23 LpC-T4P (p-Laplacian optimality), and line 24 LpC-T4H (L2 Hodge and Moore-Penrose) verified.
Lean 4 mechanization inspected. Formalizes exact cycle gauge annihilation condition <z, D p> = 0 across arbitrary finite dimension and discrete coboundary operator D.
Lean 4 mechanization inspected. Formalizes cycle flux invariance under gauge potentials and spanning cycle lower bounds.
Lean 4 mechanization inspected. Formalizes strict convexity of Lp norms and uniqueness of quotient minimizers on gauge-fixed potentials.
Lean 4 mechanization inspected. Formalizes discrete adjoint d0*, im(d0) perp ker(d0*), and Pythagorean L2 energy conservation for the Hodge-Helmholtz orthogonal decomposition.

claims.statement: For any finite graph, a cochain c is exact if and only if <y, c> = 0 for every circulation y in ker d_0^T, establishing im d_0 = (ker d_0^T)^perp independently of p.
dependencies: Finite graph 1-complex with finite-dimensional cochain spaces C^0 and C^1.
Standard inner product on edge cochains and adjoint coboundary operator d_0^T.
Finite-dimensional orthogonal complement involution (im d_0)^perp = ker d_0^T.
claims.limits: Applies to finite-dimensional graphs; infinite complexes require closed range conditions.

claims.statement: On any finite graph, vanishing circulation pairings characterize exactness via spanning-tree path integration and fundamental-cycle pairing across each connected component.
dependencies: Finite graph with arbitrary connected component and cycle structure.
Spanning forest decomposition and fundamental cycle basis construction.
Telescoping potential reconstruction along spanning tree paths.
claims.limits: Formulated on finite graphs with cycle space generated by fundamental cycles.

claims.statement: For p in (1, inf) on a finite graph with positive weights, the quotient defect minimizer is unique on the gauge-fixed subspace, yields a unique residual r_p^*, and satisfies the nonlinear graph p-Laplacian equation d_0^T(w |r_p^*|^{p-2} r_p^*) = 0.
dependencies: Finite graph with strictly positive edge weights.
Strict convexity of the power functional t -> (1/p) |t|^p for p in (1, inf).
Continuous differentiability and Euler-Lagrange stationarity on gauge-fixed potentials.
claims.limits: Applies to strictly convex regime p in (1, inf); does not apply to non-strictly convex polyhedral p = 1 or non-smooth p = inf.

claims.statement: For p = 2 on a finite graph with positive weights W, the least-squares potential is given by the Moore-Penrose formula f = L^+ d_0^T W c with L = d_0^T W d_0, selecting the minimum Euclidean-norm potential on (ker L)^perp and yielding orthogonal Hodge decomposition c = d_0 f + r.
dependencies: Finite graph with positive diagonal weight matrix W.
Normal equations L f = d_0^T W c with graph Laplacian L = d_0^T W d_0.
Solvability of normal equations via im(d_0^T W) subset im(L) and Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse L^+.
claims.limits: Applies to Hilbertian L2 regime; does not yield sparse cycle-concentrated residuals characteristic of L1.
